title: Papeles Pegados

publisher.name: Redfoxpress
publisher.location: Dugort, Achill Island, County Mayo, Ireland

description.main: A collage artist's book by the Barcelona mail artist Pere Sousa, issued as volume 141 in Redfoxpress's "C'est mon Dada" series. The 44-page hardcover glues together vintage portraiture, apparatus diagrams, and found photography.
description.extended:
Collage and mail art converge in Papeles Pegados ("Glued Papers"), the Barcelona artist Pere Sousa's contribution to Redfoxpress's C'est mon Dada series, its cover pairing old-master portraiture with a photograph of a technician adjusting a measuring apparatus.

Published in February 2020 as volume 141, the 44-page hardcover follows the series' standard A6 format (10.5 × 15 cm), thread-and-quarter-cloth bound and laser-printed on ivory paper. Sousa's spreads glue together salvaged prints, portrait photography, and diagrams of scientific instruments, working in the cut-and-paste tradition — text combined with found image — that defines the series.

Sousa (1955–2023) was a central figure in Spanish mail art: born in Pont de Suert, Catalonia, he studied sculpture at the University of Barcelona before turning to postal art in 1992. He edited P.O.BOX and Artstrike from 1994 to 2000, founded the Factoria Merz Mail archive, organized artist-stamp and mail-art exhibitions across Spain, and was recognized as one of the country's foremost sound poets for his interpretations of Kurt Schwitters.
description.artist_bio: Pere Sousa (1955-2023) was born in Pont de Suert, Catalonia, and studied sculpture and fine arts at the University of Barcelona without completing a degree. He began mail art in 1992 and, from 1994 to 2000, edited the publications P.O.BOX and Artstrike. He founded the Factoria Merz Mail archive and imprint (merzmail.net), organized artist-stamp and mail-art exhibitions including Artstrike events in Barcelona and Madrid (2000-2001), authored a chronicle of Spanish postal-art history and the book Mail Art - La Red Eterna (2011), and was recognized as one of Spain's foremost sound poets for his interpretations of Kurt Schwitters's Ursonate. His archive is held at MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art of Barcelona).

notes: No ISBN found on the publisher page or elsewhere; the cover filename uses the publication year (2020) in place of isbn13. authors[0].url is set to merzmail.net, the mail-art archive/imprint Sousa founded and authored (confirmed via multiple pages crediting him as author/organizer) - the closest equivalent to an official personal site, since he had no separate personal domain and died in 2023. This is primarily a visual/collage work with minimal running text, so language was left null.
